originalTitle: Los Angeles'ta Palisades yangınını çıkardığı suçlanan kişi mahkum edildi
titleEn: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
headline: BBC'nin haberine göre, Los Angeles'ta Palisades yangınını çıkaran kişi suçlu bulundu.
details: Olayda 12 kişi hayatını kaybetti ve 6.800'den fazla bina yıkıldı.
Jonathan Rinderknecht iki federal suçlamadan mahkum edildi.
Sanık, 17 Mart'taki duruşmada her bir suçlama için 5 ila 20 yıl hapis cezasıyle karşı karşıya.
brief: Los Angeles'ta geçen yıl ocak ayında Pacific Palisades ve Malibu'da 12 kişinin ölümüne yol açan büyük yangını çıkaran 30 yaşındaki Jonathan Rinderknecht mahkum edildi.
summary: BBC'nin aktardığına göre, ABD'nin Los Angeles şehrinde bir mahkeme, Pacific Palisades ve Malibu bölgelerinde tarihi yıkıma yol açan orman yangınını çıkaran 30 yaşındaki Jonathan Rinderknecht'i suçlu buldu. Ocak ayında meydana gelen ve 12 kişinin ölümüne, 6.800'den fazla binanın yok olmasına neden olan yangınla ilgili karar, daha önceki bir duruşmanın jürinin uzlaşamaması nedeniyle iptal edilmesinden yaklaşık beş ay sonra açıklandı. Suçlamaları reddeden sanık, iki federal suçlamadan mahkum olurken, 17 Mart'ta yapılacak duruşmada her bir suçlama için 5 ila 20 yıl hapis cezası istemiyle hakim karşısına çıkacak. Savcılık deliller arasında konum verileri ve güvenlik kamerası kayıtlarına yer verirken, savunma avukatları yeterli fiziksel delil bulunmadığını savundu.

sourceText: BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat US & Canada Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles Image source, Apu Gomes/Getty Images Image caption, Homes along Los Angeles' Sunset Boulevard could be seen engulfed in flames during the fires of January 2025 A jury in Los Angeles has found a 30-year-old man guilty of starting one of the most destructive wildfires in California's history. Jonathan Rinderknecht was convicted of arson after starting the fires that swept through Pacific Palisades and parts of Malibu in January last year, killing 12 people and destroying more than 6,800 buildings in the US state. The conviction was handed down nearly five months after deadlocked jurors led to the judge declaring a mistrial . Rinderknecht, who had pleaded not guilty, was convicted of two federal charges. He is due to be sentenced on 17 March when he faces between five and 20 years in prison on each charge. Image source, US Attorney for the Central District of California Image caption, Jonathan Rinderknecht's arrest in October last year Rinderknecht was found guilty of lighting a fire on 1 January last year which burned undetected deep in root systems before flaring back up six days later. One of the charges was for starting the original brush fire, while the other centred on the damage caused when it reignited into a catastrophic blaze. "We were determined to hold him accountable, and today's guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended," said Bill Essayli, who leads the US Attorney's Office for the Central District of California. Defence attorney Steve Haney had argued at trial that prosecutors lacked sufficient physical evidence or records to prove their case. Lawyers for the defendant said they were "disappointed" by the verdict but respected the jury's decision. Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who was widely criticised for her handling of the fires, said in a statement that "no verdict can bring back the lives lost or erase the pain families have endured". "So many are still struggling to rebuild," she said. "For those still displaced, the devastation remains a daily reality." Prosecutors had argued that Rinderknecht was driven by revenge, anger and loneliness because he had nowhere to go for the holiday. They cited geolocation data from his iPhone, security camera footage that showed his car's location and witness testimony from passengers.
